payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: the small gray rubber cylinder becomes brown
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the small gray rubber cylinder visibly brown in the edited image, rather than remaining gray as in the source?
node.criteria: Pass if the target cylinder’s visible color changes from gray in the source to brown in the edited image. Fail if it remains gray or is visibly another color. Unknown if the target or its color cannot be reliably observed.
node.binding: The target cylinder must become brown.
node.source_quote: the small gray rubber cylinder becomes brown
node.endpoint: The target cylinder is visibly brown.
node.necessity: The instruction explicitly requests a gray-to-brown color change; without the brown endpoint, the requested change is incomplete.

node_traces.evidence: The small upright cylinder just right of the brown sphere is gray in the source and visibly brown in the edited image, including its side and rim.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s binding is too generic to distinguish the requested small gray rubber cylinder from nearby objects, and the traces expose a specific identity ambiguity: the edited brown object is interpreted as hollow, while the source target appears solid. Refine the binding using stable source-image cues (the small upright gray cylinder just right of the brown sphere) and make the criterion explicitly compare that same object across source and edit. Keep object identity separate from the color endpoint: a hollow appearance should not by itself negate visible brown progress unless the evidence establishes it is a different object or that the target’s identity cannot be resolved. If identity remains uncertain, report unresolved rather than converting uncertainty into a confident failure. The repeated pass/fail variation is a robustness signal, not evidence that the color edit is absent; seek consistent evidence for the target’s identity and visible color. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported."}
